newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah firm on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah firm on tight liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah held firm on Monday as a public holiday in the United States kept market interest pinned on domestic money market liquidity.
Dealers in Jakarta said the money market opened at 18 percent as no alternative financing was available through overnight swaps due to the U.S. holiday.
Overnight money later eased to 15.0/16.0 percent because liquidity was not as tight as feared initially, dealers said.

One state bank dealer said liquidity concerns dragged spot dollars slightly lower to 2,321.0/21.40 at 0210 GMT from an opening of 2,321.25/22.00. Dollar/rupiah was quoted at 2,321.10/21.60 at 0450 GMT.

"Sentiment on the rupiah remains firm. Operators also appeared to keep their distance from the central bank floor rate on speculation that it may raise the band by one point this afternoon," one Japanese bank dealer said.
Dealers said the market was keeping a watchful eye on liquidity conditions ahead of Tuesday's weekly tax payments and bank liquidity reports.

A U.S. bank dealer said Singapore operators were initially nervous on Friday's news that an angry mob set fire to churches and other buildings in eastern Java, but a calm Jakarta market seemed to have eased fears.
Spot rupiah fell briefly to a low of 2,323.25 on Friday on the news before it settled around 2,320.5/21.0 at close in Jakarta.

"It depends on whether the situation escalates. If not, it's pretty much viewed as a contained affair," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore. "There probably won't be any spillover, especially as the tom/nexts are very high today."
Dealers said longer-term swap rates remained expensive due to high short-dated swap rates, which rose on expectations of continued tight liquidity.

In Thailand, the baht weakened slightly in slow trade in line with the dollar's firm tone and low domestic interest rates. It was quoted at 25.458-25.462 at 0452 GMT against 25.446-25.451 late on Friday.

The Thai overnight interbank rate edged up a notch but remained low in early trade as liquidity was slightly tighter due to holidays in some foreign markets, which reduced the availability of offshore funds.
"The interbank rate will stay at around 7.00 percent today. Most banks still have excess funds. This will hinder the interbank rate from any sharp rise," said a foreign bank dealer in Bangkok.
The Malaysian ringgit regained some ground as players covered their short positions, but dealers said commercial demand for the dollar would limit the ringgit's upside.
"I think there'll be some buying (of the dollar) at the 2.5000 level," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore.
"Everything turned out quite well in the UMNO (United Malays National Organisation) elections, so people are putting some money back in Malaysia," he added.
The release of Malaysia's August industrial production data had little immediate impact.
The Singapore dollar was also unmoved by the release of data showing August money supply rose 6.4 percent year on year.
Dealers said the market was bracing itself for more signs of economic weakness following last week's news August industrial production fell 7.6 percent year on year.
"Most people are forecasting a quite drastic slowdown so it's probably priced in," said the U.S. bank dealer.
He said the U.S. dollar would have trouble rising above selling interest at S$1.4120 unless it headed sharply higher against the mark and yen.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
